_sftp_when_migrated._why: Ready to swap in once knocbrac.com moves to 34sp's newer cluster (requested Oct 2026). The OLD cluster has no ssh/sftp at all: `mkdir .ssh` over sftp returns Permission denied on /, so key auth was never going to work regardless of the OpenSSH 5.3 / ssh-rsa problem. Keep ssh_options when swapping — the new cluster may still be old enough to need it. Verify first: sftp -b /dev/null -o BatchMode=yes -o PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms=+ssh-rsa -P 22 knocbraccom@ftp.knocbrac.com must exit 0.

_notes: sftpcli (system OpenSSH, zero Python deps) over port 22, KEY AUTH REQUIRED: sftp runs with BatchMode=yes so it cannot prompt for a password. THE HOST RUNS OpenSSH 5.3 (verified 11 Oct 2026), which can only sign with ssh-rsa (SHA-1); OpenSSH 8.8+ clients disable that by default and will load your key then DISCARD it, reporting 'Permission denied (publickey,password)' as though no key existed. Hence ssh_options above — do not remove it. An ed25519 or ECDSA key cannot help: 5.3 predates both (6.5 and 5.7). One-time setup: ssh-copy-id -o PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms=+ssh-rsa -p 22 knocbraccom@ftp.knocbrac.com. If the account turns out to be sftp-only (no shell), ssh-copy-id will fail — then install the key by hand over sftp: mkdir .ssh, put ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub .ssh/authorized_keys, chmod 700 .ssh, chmod 600 .ssh/authorized_keys. Readiness test that matches what deploy actually does: sftp -b /dev/null -o BatchMode=yes -o PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms=+ssh-rsa -P 22 knocbraccom@ftp.knocbrac.com (must exit 0). The HOSTNAME works on port 22 — the old note claiming the IP (80.82.113.174) was required was wrong; both answer and both offer publickey. Batches every upload into one sftp session, which beats FTP's per-file STOR when the line is throttled. Fallbacks if keys ever break: transport=sftp (paramiko + password, needs pip install paramiko), or back to transport=ftp with host=ftp.knocbrac.com and use_tls=false — note FTPS login 530s on this host and plain FTP sends the password in clear text.
